title: wc_crypto2dev_init idempotent guard misses mutex and pool re-init after cleanup
description: wc_crypto2dev_init() has 'if (g_crypto2dev_fd >= 0) return 0' as its early-return guard. After wc_crypto2dev_cleanup() is called: g_crypto2dev_fd is set to -1, g_pool_inited is set to 0, g_ecdsa_fd_lock_inited is set to 0. A second call to wc_crypto2dev_init() will proceed to re-init the mutex with 'if (\!g_ecdsa_fd_lock_inited) { wc_InitMutex(...); }' — correct. But: the init guard checks g_crypto2dev_fd BEFORE the mutex is initialized. Between cleanup and re-init there is a window where g_ecdsa_fd_lock_inited=0 and g_pool_inited=0, so the second init works. However, if wc_crypto2dev_init() is called concurrently (two threads racing to init), both pass the 'fd < 0' check simultaneously, both call open() and both call wc_InitMutex(). The second InitMutex on the same global is undefined behavior on pthreads. The documented 'call before spawning threads' requirement partially covers this, but the guard itself is racy by design.
